questions.q: Change of one type of differentiated epithelium into another, as in a smoker's bronchus, is called:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Columnar to squamous metaplasia.

questions.q: Aconitum napellus is commonly known as:
questions.why: Aconitum napellus (Ranunculaceae) is monkshood or wolf's bane; deadly nightshade is Belladonna, foxglove Digitalis and thorn apple Stramonium.

questions.q: A 'chocolate cyst' of the ovary is characteristic of:
questions.why: An endometrioma contains old altered blood that looks like chocolate.

questions.q: Sticky, stringy, tough mucus that can be drawn into long threads, as in sinusitis or bronchitis, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Kali bich: ropy discharges, pains in small spots.

questions.q: The word 'rubric' comes from the Latin for:
opts: red, because old books printed headings in red ink
questions.why: Rubrica means red; headings were once printed in red, so a repertory heading is a rubric.

questions.q: Maceration and percolation are methods used to prepare:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. The plant material is soaked (maceration) or extracted by slow filtration of solvent (percolation).

questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. While translating Cullen's Materia Medica in 1790 he took cinchona himself and developed symptoms like intermittent fever.
